pr_summary: The CI pipelines for LightGBM use `pip install --user` which causes cross-job contamination in hosted runners. The user-site directory persists across CI jobs, leading to stale package installations. The fix removes `--user` flags from pip install commands in `.ci/test.sh` and `.ci/test_windows.ps1` to ensure each CI job installs the freshly built wheel into the isolated Conda environment.
platform_constraint_evidence: .ci/test.sh is a bash script for Linux/macOS CI
.ci/test_windows.ps1 is for Windows but the fix is cross-platform
GitHub Actions workflows run on ubuntu-latest, macos-13, and windows
python-package/pyproject.toml classifiers include Linux, macOS, Windows
LightGBM is a cross-platform ML framework with no Windows/macOS-only restrictions for the Python package
notes: LightGBM is a gradient boosting framework with Python, R, and C++ interfaces. The Python package uses scikit-build-core for building CMake-based native extensions. The project uses conda/mamba for CI environment management with pip for package installation. The fix removes --user flags to prevent cross-job contamination in CI. The project is fully cross-platform and can be built/tested in a Linux x86-64 container. Python 3.7+ is supported, with CI testing Python 3.7-3.11.
